model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a typed, checkable vocabulary of socio-operational dependency relations that can be mixed into any host subject record, stating what a subject relies on among processes, capabilities, people, organizations, suppliers, agreements, funds, time windows, places and jurisdictions, with declared direction, endpoint constraints, evidence and refutation tests.
model.scope_statement: Socio-operational split of WM-XCT-037. Owns the taxonomy of dependency kinds whose depended-on endpoint is a human, organizational, procedural, contractual, legal, financial or situational entity, plus the declaration discipline (direction, endpoint constraints, cardinality, applicability, evidence grade, false-positive tests, disposition) that makes such an assertion falsifiable. It carries references and bindings to the models that own the endpoints; it never restates their content, lifecycle or consequences, and never executes workflows, contracts, payments, staffing, procurement or legal decisions.
in_scope: Process and activity reliance kinds, including separation of BPMN-style ordering from a declared reliance
Capability, competence, qualification and authorisation-to-perform reliance bound to governed classification concepts
Organizational, unit, post and role-holder reliance kept distinct from ownership, consolidation and reporting structure
Supplier, third-party, direct/indirect business-partner and subcontracting-chain reliance, including chain position and substitutability inputs
Separation of normative obligation from operational reliance, recorded as citation plus binding
Financial and resource reliance strands: funding, revenue, payment settlement, workforce capacity, material resources
Temporal, spatial and jurisdictional reliance qualifiers, including required lead time, site binding and authorisation dependence
Per-kind direction, endpoint type constraints, cardinality, cycle and transitivity rules, and applicability conditions
Evidence basis, evidence grade, asserter attribution and the four discrimination tests (ownership, sequence, correlation, obligation)
Disposition of withdrawn, refuted, expired and superseded assertions
out_of_scope: Technical, system, component, interface and data-flow dependency typing (adjacent split of this model)
Impact severity computation, criticality scoring, business impact analysis targets such as MTD/RTO/RPO, and impact propagation algorithms
Risk identification, risk evaluation, risk treatment and risk register maintenance
The text, lifecycle, remedies and interpretation of contracts, statutes and policies
Organizational structure, ownership hierarchy, membership and reporting-line mastering
Process model authoring and process model repositories
Supplier onboarding, procurement decisions, contract award, staffing decisions, payment execution and supervisory submission
Runtime evaluation, enforcement and audit-trail storage, immutability and review
Setting retention periods and executing physical erasure

boundary_notes.neighbor: Technical / system dependency graph (adjacent split of WM-XCT-037)
boundary_notes.distinction: That split types endpoints that are components, interfaces, data stores and network paths. This split only types endpoints that are people, organizations, processes, capabilities, agreements, funds, time, place or jurisdiction. An ICT service is referenced here as an arrangement with a party, not as a technical component.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Business impact analysis and continuity model
boundary_notes.distinction: BIA identifies resource requirements and sets recovery objectives; this model declares the reliance edge, its evidence and its applicability. Recovery targets, impact severity and prioritisation are consumed from, not defined by, this model.

Duties, permissions, prohibitions, remedies and their fulfilment state belong to the instrument model. This model records only a citation to the instrument, the deontic class asserted there, and whether operational reliance survives the duty's removal.

Sub-organization, unit, post, membership and accounting-consolidating parenthood are mastered there. This model asserts reliance on those entities and must not re-derive or restate the structural graph.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Third-party arrangement register and supervisory reporting
boundary_notes.distinction: Compilation of a read-only extract is in scope; the arrangement master record, the supervisory obligation, its interpretation and any submission are not.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Records management, privacy and audit model
boundary_notes.distinction: This model states that dispositioned assertions must be retained as tombstones and emits attribution entries. Retention periods, erasure execution and audit-trail integrity are owned by the adopting Dimension's records, privacy and audit models.

sources.title: Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN), Version 2.0.2
sources.relevance: Normative distinction between Sequence Flow (ordering of flow elements inside one process) and Message Flow (exchange across participant/pool boundaries), plus associations and data associations. Grounds the process-reliance kind and the sequence-is-not-causation rule.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Organization, FormalOrganization, OrganizationalUnit, Post, Role, Membership with memberDuring, subOrganizationOf, hasUnit, reportsTo, headOf, hasSite. The Recommendation explicitly removed the claim that the org:reportsTo graph is acyclic, which forces per-kind cycle rules here.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) and Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC)
sources.version_or_date: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft, 15 November 2022 (last Recommendation-stage version 19 October 2017)
sources.relevance: Allen interval relations (before, after, meets, overlaps, during, starts, finishes, equals and inverses) for temporal reliance. Cited as alignment only: the ontology asserts temporal topology and makes no causal claim, and its current /TR/ version is not at Recommendation stage.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Duty, Permission, Prohibition, Constraint, Party, assigner/assignee and the separation of a normative rule from its fulfilment. Grounds the obligation-versus-reliance distinction and the deontic class code.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: prov:wasInfluencedBy as a deliberately non-causal superproperty, the qualified-influence specialization pattern, wasAttributedTo and actedOnBehalfOf. Grounds assertion attribution and the correlation-is-not-dependency rule.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: Article 3(22) 'critical or important function' as a materiality test on functions rather than assets; register of information covering arrangements including subcontracting (Article 28); preliminary assessment of concentration and of further subcontracting, including third-country subcontractors (Article 29). Worked example of function-scoped and jurisdiction-sensitive dependency typing.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2024/1760 on corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: 'Chain of activities' with explicit upstream and limited downstream reach, direct and indirect business partners, and carve-outs (product disposal; downstream excluded for regulated financial undertakings). Demonstrates that chain scope is instrument-specific and must be declared per assertion.

sources.title: European Legislation Identifier (ELI) register
sources.organization: Publications Office of the European Union / EUR-Lex
sources.relevance: URI-based identification of legal acts, FRBR-based metadata including jurisdiction and adoption date, and an ontology for exchanging legislation metadata. Supplies a jurisdiction-neutral citation mechanism for legal and jurisdictional reliance.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1, Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Practice evidence for sub-tier supplier visibility, criticality analysis and dependency mapping across supply chain levels; also marks the boundary where technical supply chain dependency is handled by the adjacent split.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Business impact analysis practice: identify resource requirements and interdependencies, then set recovery objectives. Used to fix the boundary that this model declares reliance while the BIA sets impact and recovery targets. Cited as dated practice guidance, not as a current requirement.

sources.title: Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight - A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities
sources.relevance: Cross-jurisdictional common terminology for critical third-party services, identification of systemic third-party dependencies and concentration, explicitly aiming at comparable and interoperable approaches across jurisdictions.

sources.title: Level 2 Data: Who Owns Whom
sources.version_or_date: Relationship Record CDF format 2.1; Level 2 collection began May 2017; consulted 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: Direct and ultimate accounting consolidating parent relationships plus reporting-exception formats. The canonical counterexample proving that ownership and consolidation are not dependency, and that absence of a parent record is not absence of reliance.

sources.title: Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02)
sources.version_or_date: EBA/GL/2019/02, published 4 March 2019, applicable from 30 September 2019
sources.relevance: A definition of outsourcing that separates outsourced functions from other third-party arrangements such as purchase of goods, and criteria for critical or important functions plus register expectations. Grounds the arrangement-type code.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.version_or_date: RFC 3339, Proposed Standard, July 2002 (updated by RFC 9557)
sources.relevance: Profile of ISO 8601 requiring an explicit relationship to UTC: the Z designator or a numeric offset, with -00:00 reserved for a known UTC instant whose local offset is unknown. Grounds the timestamp rule and the event/observation time split.

sources.title: UN/CEFACT Web Vocabularies
sources.organization: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) / UN/CEFACT
sources.version_or_date: Buy-Ship-Pay Reference Data Model vocabulary, version D23B; consulted 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: Linked-data representation of the Buy-Ship-Pay Reference Data Model and UN/LOCODE. Separating the buy, ship and pay strands is the basis for distinguishing a payment/settlement reliance from a delivery reliance from a contractual reliance on the same counterparty.

sources.title: ESCO - European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations classification
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion
sources.relevance: Governed occupation, skill/competence and knowledge concepts with mappings to the International Standard Classification of Occupations, giving stable endpoint identifiers for capability and competence reliance instead of free-text role names.

sources.title: ISO 17442: The LEI Code Structure
sources.version_or_date: ISO 17442 Part 1 published 2012, Part 2 published 2019; page consulted 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: A 20-character globally governed legal entity identifier where each code represents exactly one entity. Supplies the second tier of identity priority for party endpoints when no master-system identifier governs the counterparty.

bundles.name: Socio-operational dependency kind taxonomy
bundles.description: The catalogue of dependency kinds whose depended-on endpoint is an activity, capability, actor, arrangement, obligation, resource, time window, place or jurisdiction, each with its own endpoint rules and discriminating evidence.
bundles.rationale: No single authority types socio-operational reliance. BPMN types intra-process ordering and cross-participant messaging, W3C ORG types structural and reporting relations, ODRL types duties, DORA and CSDDD type third-party and chain reliance with different scopes, and UN/CEFACT separates buy, ship and pay strands. An untyped 'depends on' edge silently merges these, so the taxonomy must be assembled explicitly and each kind must carry its own falsification test.

layers.name: Work and capability reliance
layers.description: Kinds whose depended-on endpoint is work to be performed: an activity or process step, or a capability, competence, qualification or authorisation that makes performance possible.

findings.name: Process and activity reliance, and the sequence-is-not-causation rule
findings.description: A process dependency asserts that an activity cannot start, continue or complete without a specific output, decision or message from another activity or participant. BPMN sequence flow orders flow elements within one process and message flow crosses participant boundaries; neither is a causal claim, and Allen interval relations order intervals without asserting causation. This finding fixes when an observed ordering may be promoted to a declared reliance and what blocking mode applies.

questions.text: Which modelled construct grounds this reliance: an intra-process sequence flow, a cross-participant message flow, a data association, or none of these?
answer_data: Reference to the source process model and element identifier

questions.text: What specific output, decision or message does the dependent activity consume from the depended-on activity?
If the depended-on activity does not complete, is the effect a hard stop, a degraded continuation, or a documented manual workaround?
answer_data: Workaround description and its own preconditions
Tolerance window before the effect bites

questions.text: What evidence separates this from mere observed ordering: a modelled flow, a written procedure, or only historical co-occurrence?
For which process version, variant or participant lane does this assertion hold?

data_elements.name: Depended-on activity reference
data_elements.description: Governed reference to the activity, task or process step relied upon, resolved in the owning process model repository.

data_elements.name: Flow construct code
data_elements.description: Code recording which BPMN-style construct grounds the reliance: sequence flow, message flow, data association, or unmodelled.

data_elements.name: Blocking mode code
data_elements.description: Effect of non-performance on the dependent activity: hard-blocking, degrading, or advisory.

data_elements.name: Consumed output reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the output, decision or message that the dependent activity consumes.

data_elements.name: Process variant scope
data_elements.description: Process version, variant or lane for which the assertion is claimed to hold.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The finding contributes typed relation semantics and reference data carried on the host subject record. The process models, procedures and execution logs that supply the evidence are artifacts of the process-model and operations neighbours; producing a local copy would duplicate a target-owned artifact and would drift from its version.

findings.name: Capability, competence and authorisation-to-perform reliance
findings.description: Reliance on an ability to perform rather than on a named holder: a capability concept, a skill or competence, a qualification, or an authorisation or licence that permits performance. ESCO supplies governed occupation, skill and knowledge concepts mapped to ISCO, so the endpoint is a concept identifier rather than free text. Regulatory function tests such as the DORA critical-or-important-function materiality test show that the dependent side is often a function, not a system.

questions.text: Is the depended-on endpoint a capability concept, a qualification, or an authorisation to perform, and how is each defined here?
Which governed classification concept identifies the capability or competence, and at which scheme version?
answer_data: Local extension flag where no governed concept exists

questions.text: What minimum proficiency, coverage or number of qualified holders must exist for the dependent function to remain performable?
answer_data: Coverage window such as shift or region

questions.text: Is the dependent endpoint classified as a critical or important function under a cited regulatory test, and which test is applied?
answer_data: Citation of the applied test with jurisdiction

questions.text: What substitution, delegation or temporary derogation is recognised when the capability is unavailable, and what does it not cover?
answer_data: Explicit exclusions and approval authority reference

data_elements.name: Capability concept reference
data_elements.description: Governed concept identifier for the capability, skill, knowledge or qualification relied upon.

data_elements.name: Capability scheme version
data_elements.description: Name and version of the classification scheme from which the concept is drawn.

data_elements.name: Minimum qualified holders
data_elements.description: Minimum number of holders with the capability required for the dependent function to remain performable.

data_elements.name: Authorisation required flag
data_elements.description: Whether performance additionally requires an authorisation, licence or registration beyond the competence itself.

data_elements.name: Function criticality code
data_elements.description: Classification of the dependent function under a cited regulatory or internal criticality test, with the test recorded separately.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Capability reliance resolves to governed concept references plus thresholds held on the host record. The competence catalogue, qualification records and authorisation certificates are mastered by the classification authority and by the workforce and licensing models; reproducing them here would create a competing register.

layers.name: Actor, arrangement and obligation reliance
layers.description: Kinds whose depended-on endpoint is an organization, unit, post, role holder, business partner, arrangement, or a normative rule cited from a contract, statute or policy.

findings.name: Organizational, post and role reliance separated from ownership and reporting
findings.description: W3C ORG models subOrganizationOf, hasUnit, reportsTo, Post, Role and time-bounded Membership; GLEIF Level 2 models direct and ultimate accounting consolidating parents. None of these is a dependency: a parent may supply nothing, and an unrelated supplier may be indispensable. This finding declares the reliance edge on an actor at a stated granularity and holds the tests that keep it distinct from control, ownership and reporting structure.

questions.text: Which identifier identifies the depended-on actor: a legal entity identifier, an internal organizational unit identifier, or a post identifier?
answer_data: Fallback identifier tier used and why

questions.text: Is the asserted edge a reliance on the actor's performance, or a structural, ownership or reporting relation already mastered elsewhere?
answer_data: Reference to the structural relation that was ruled out
Outcome of the ownership discrimination test

questions.text: At what granularity is the reliance asserted: legal entity, organizational unit, post, or the individual holder of a post?
answer_data: Justification for asserting below unit level
Aggregation rule to the next level up

questions.text: Who owns the depended-on actor record, and does a change of ownership or consolidation alter the reliance claim?
How is the reliance re-evaluated when the post is vacant, the unit is merged, or the holder changes?

data_elements.name: Actor endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Governed reference to the depended-on organization, unit, post or holder.

data_elements.name: Actor granularity code
data_elements.description: Level at which the reliance is asserted: legal entity, organizational unit, post, or individual holder.

data_elements.name: Structural relation excluded flag
data_elements.description: Records that the assertion was tested against, and is not merely, a sub-organization, consolidation or reporting relation.

data_elements.name: Vacancy handling note
data_elements.description: Rule applied when a depended-on post is vacant or its holder changes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The output is a typed edge plus discrimination flags attached to the host record. Organization charts, membership records and ownership hierarchies are artifacts of the organization register and of the LEI system; generating a local organizational artifact would duplicate a target-owned master and invite divergence.

findings.name: Supplier, third-party and subcontracting-chain reliance
findings.description: Reliance on external parties, distinguishing outsourcing of a function from purchase of goods or services and from informal reliance, recording chain position for direct and indirect partners and nth-tier subcontractors, and capturing substitutability as an assessment input. Scope differs by instrument: a CSDDD chain of activities excludes product disposal and, for regulated financial undertakings, downstream activities, while a DORA register of information covers ICT arrangements including subcontracting; the same counterparty can therefore be in one scope and outside another.

questions.text: Is the arrangement outsourcing of a function, a purchase of goods or services, or a reliance with no contract at all?
answer_data: Arrangement master record reference where one exists

questions.text: What is the depended-on party's chain position, direct partner, indirect partner or nth-tier subcontractor, and through which intermediate parties?
How substitutable is the party, measured on what scale, and over what switching period?
answer_data: Named alternatives and their own dependencies

questions.text: Which external register or reporting schema must this record populate, and what mandatory fields does that schema impose?
Which contractual right or supervisory power permits visibility into the sub-tier, and where does that right end?
answer_data: Scope and limits of the visibility right
Evidence that the sub-tier data was obtained under it

data_elements.name: Arrangement type code
data_elements.description: Classification of the arrangement as outsourcing of a function, purchase of goods or services, or non-contractual reliance.

data_elements.name: Arrangement reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the arrangement or contract record in the owning master system.

data_elements.name: Chain position ordinal
data_elements.description: Hop count from the asserting subject to the depended-on party; one denotes a direct business partner.

data_elements.name: Intermediate party reference
data_elements.description: Ordered references to parties standing between the subject and the depended-on party.

data_elements.name: Substitutability measure
data_elements.description: Assessed replaceability of the party with its scale, unit and switching period; an input to, not a result of, risk evaluation.

data_elements.name: Supported function reference
data_elements.description: The subject-side function or activity that the external party supports.

artifacts.name: Third-party dependency register extract
artifacts.description: A read-only extract for one reporting scope listing depended-on parties, arrangement type, chain position, intermediate parties, supported functions and substitutability inputs, shaped so that it can populate an external arrangement or outsourcing register without this model interpreting the underlying obligation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each row is keyed by the arrangement identifier issued by the authoritative arrangement master system, plus the depended-on party's ISO 17442 legal entity identifier where one exists and a Dimension-assigned ULID only where neither is available. The extract itself is identified by scope key plus a monotonic sequence number and the kind-profile version; the reporting reference instant is carried as metadata and is never part of the identifier.

findings.name: Normative obligation distinguished from operational reliance
findings.description: An obligation is a deontic statement: a duty owed by or to a party under a contract, statute or policy, with an assigner, an assignee and a fulfilment condition. Operational reliance is a factual statement that performance fails without a counterparty's act. They frequently co-occur but are independent: a redundant duty can exist with no reliance, and an informal accommodation can create reliance with no duty. This finding carries only the citation, the deontic class asserted at the source, and the outcome of the independence test; the rule's text, remedies and fulfilment state stay with the instrument model.

questions.text: Is the asserted item a duty, a condition attached to a permission or prohibition, or a purely factual operational reliance?
Which legal act, contract clause or policy statement is cited, by governed identifier and version?
answer_data: Instrument identifier such as an ELI URI or contract clause reference

questions.text: Which party bears the duty and which benefits, and does that direction match the direction of the operational reliance?
answer_data: Direction agreement flag with explanation where they diverge

questions.text: What consequence does the cited rule attach to non-performance, and is that consequence recorded here or owned by the instrument model?
answer_data: Consequence summary as a pointer only
Explicit statement that this model records no fulfilment state

questions.text: What test shows whether removing the obligation would remove the operational reliance?
answer_data: Test description and date of execution

data_elements.name: Normative instrument reference
data_elements.description: Governed citation to the legal act, contract clause or policy statement that creates the duty.

data_elements.name: Deontic class code
data_elements.description: Class of the cited rule at its source: duty, permission condition, or prohibition condition.

data_elements.name: Obligated party reference
data_elements.description: Party bearing the duty under the cited rule, recorded to test direction agreement with the reliance edge.

data_elements.name: Reliance independent of duty flag
data_elements.description: Whether the operational reliance survives removal of the cited obligation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately produces only citations, a deontic class code and a test outcome. Materialising an obligation artifact here would reproduce the instrument model's content and would risk presenting a derived summary as the operative legal text across jurisdictions with different interpretive rules.

layers.name: Resource, time, place and jurisdiction reliance
layers.description: Kinds whose depended-on endpoint is a fund, revenue stream, payment settlement, workforce or material resource, or a situational condition of time, location or jurisdiction.

findings.name: Financial and non-financial resource reliance
findings.description: Reliance on funding, revenue concentration, payment settlement, workforce capacity or material resources. The UN/CEFACT Buy-Ship-Pay model separates the buy, ship and pay strands, so reliance on a counterparty for settlement is a different assertion from reliance on the same counterparty for delivery or for the underlying agreement. Business impact analysis practice supplies the resource-requirement framing. Accounting recognition and any payment execution are excluded.

questions.text: Which resource strand is relied upon: funding or budget, revenue, payment settlement, workforce capacity, or physical material?
answer_data: Note where several strands run to the same counterparty

questions.text: What quantity, share or concentration figure expresses the reliance, in which unit and over which period?
Does the reliance run to a named counterparty, to a specific instrument or facility, or to an aggregate pool?
answer_data: Aggregation basis where a pool is used

questions.text: What resource state does the reliance assume: committed, contingent, discretionary, or withdrawn?
answer_data: Trigger that would change the state

questions.text: Which contingency, reserve or alternative source is recognised, and what does it explicitly not cover?

data_elements.name: Resource strand code
data_elements.description: Strand of resource reliance: funding, revenue, settlement, workforce capacity, or material.

data_elements.name: Reliance share
data_elements.description: Quantified share or concentration expressing the extent of reliance, with unit.

data_elements.name: Measurement period
data_elements.description: Period over which the reliance share is measured.

data_elements.name: Resource state code
data_elements.description: Assumed state of the relied-upon resource: committed, contingent, discretionary, or withdrawn.

data_elements.name: Alternative source reference
data_elements.description: References to recognised contingency, reserve or alternative resource sources.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Resource reliance is expressed as coded strands, measures and references held on the host record. Ledgers, budgets, funding agreements and workforce plans are mastered by finance and workforce models, and any figure restated here would be a stale copy of a controlled financial record.

findings.name: Temporal, spatial and jurisdictional reliance
findings.description: Three situational kinds. Temporal reliance binds the subject to a window, deadline, calendar or required lead time, expressed with Allen interval relations for topology and RFC 3339 instants for endpoints. Spatial reliance binds it to a site, access route or co-location using governed location codes. Jurisdictional reliance binds it to an authorisation, recognition or applicable-law condition of a named jurisdiction, cited by governed legal identifier. DORA's specific concern with subcontractors established in a third country is an example that jurisdictional reliance is material; it is used as an instance, not as universal doctrine.

questions.text: What temporal relation is asserted between which two intervals, and is a minimum lead time required?
answer_data: Temporal relation code drawn from the interval relation set
Required lead time as a duration

questions.text: Which governed location or site identifier bounds the reliance, and does the reliance survive relocation of that site?
answer_data: Location code and code list version
Site reference in the owning facility model

questions.text: Is the jurisdictional element an authorisation to operate, a recognition or equivalence, a localisation constraint, or a choice of governing law?
What becomes of the assertion when the window closes, the site becomes unavailable, or the authorisation lapses?
Which code lists are used for country, subdivision and location, and at which versions?
answer_data: Handling of codes with no governed equivalent

data_elements.name: Temporal relation code
data_elements.description: Interval relation asserted between the dependent and depended-on intervals, drawn from the standard thirteen elementary relations.

data_elements.name: Required lead time
data_elements.description: Minimum interval that must elapse between the depended-on event and the dependent activity.

data_elements.name: Validity interval
data_elements.description: Interval over which the assertion holds, with both bounds expressed as RFC 3339 instants carrying seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Location code
data_elements.description: Governed location or site code bounding a spatial reliance, with its code list version recorded.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction code
data_elements.description: Code for the jurisdiction whose authorisation, recognition or law the reliance depends upon, stated relative to a named reference frame.

data_elements.name: Jurisdictional basis reference
data_elements.description: Citation to the instrument or authorisation creating the jurisdictional reliance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are qualifiers on an assertion rather than deliverables: coded relations, instants, location codes and citations. Licences, permits, site records and legal texts are artifacts of the licensing, facility and legal-instrument models, and copying them would import one jurisdiction's document form into a jurisdiction-neutral model.

bundles.name: Declaration discipline for socio-operational dependencies
bundles.description: The rules that make a typed socio-operational assertion checkable and refutable: per-kind direction, endpoint constraints, cardinality, cycle and transitivity rules, applicability conditions, evidence grading, discrimination tests and disposition.
bundles.rationale: A taxonomy without endpoint and direction rules yields edges that cannot be validated or refuted. PROV models influence rather than causation and supplies a qualified pattern for attributing an assertion to an agent, W3C ORG demonstrates that a plausible acyclicity assumption had to be withdrawn from a published vocabulary, and supervisory guidance expects a declared dependency to trace to a basis rather than to inference.

layers.name: Relation semantics and applicability
layers.description: Per-kind declaration of dependent and depended-on endpoint types, direction, cardinality, cycle and transitivity behaviour, applicability conditions and external alignments.

findings.name: Direction, endpoint constraints, cardinality and applicability per kind
findings.description: Every kind in the taxonomy declares its permitted dependent and depended-on endpoint types, its canonical direction, whether an inverse is derived rather than stored, cardinality on each side, whether cycles are permitted, whether the relation is transitive across chain hops, and the conditions under which the assertion applies at all. The specialization pattern of a non-causal influence superproperty supplies the modelling idiom, the withdrawal of the reportsTo acyclicity claim shows that cycle behaviour must be declared and not assumed, and the sequence-versus-message distinction shows that endpoint scope differs by kind.

questions.text: For this kind, which dependent and depended-on endpoint types are permitted, and which are explicitly forbidden?
answer_data: Permitted endpoint type list per side
Forbidden endpoint type list with reasons
Owning model for each endpoint type

questions.text: What cardinality applies on each side of this kind, and is a cycle permitted?
answer_data: Cycle permitted flag with handling rule
Validation behaviour when the constraint is breached

questions.text: Is this kind transitive across chain hops, and if not, how must multi-hop reliance be declared?
Which conditions must hold for an assertion of this kind to be applicable, and what renders it inapplicable?
answer_data: Default disposition when a condition fails

questions.text: Which external property or definition does this kind align to, and at exactly which point does the alignment stop?
answer_data: External property or term identifier with version
Alignment type such as broader, narrower or related
Explicit non-conformance note where semantics diverge

data_elements.name: Kind identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the dependency kind within the owning Dimension namespace.

data_elements.name: Kind profile version
data_elements.description: Ordered version label of the profile under which an assertion was made; never a date used as identity.

data_elements.name: Permitted endpoint types
data_elements.description: Declared endpoint type sets for the dependent and depended-on sides of the kind.

data_elements.name: Cardinality constraint
data_elements.description: Cardinality expression for each side of the relation as declared by the profile.

data_elements.name: Transitivity flag
data_elements.description: Whether consumers may infer a multi-hop edge for this kind.

data_elements.name: Cycle permitted flag
data_elements.description: Whether cycles are permitted for this kind, following the explicit withdrawal of a general acyclicity assumption in published organizational vocabularies.

data_elements.name: Alignment mapping
data_elements.description: Mappings from the kind to external properties or terms, with the version and the point at which the alignment ceases to hold.

artifacts.name: Dependency kind profile
artifacts.description: The versioned, machine-readable declaration of one dependency kind: endpoint types per side, canonical direction, cardinality, cycle and transitivity behaviour, applicability conditions, required evidence grade, applicable false-positive tests, and external alignment mappings with their limits.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the kind identifier minted in the owning Dimension package namespace, expressed as a stable IRI where the Dimension publishes one, paired with an ordered version label. The owning package is identified by its master-system identifier and, where it is a legal entity, its ISO 17442 identifier. Publication and review dates are metadata and never form part of the identifier.

layers.name: Evidence, discrimination and refutation
layers.description: The basis on which a socio-operational dependency may be declared, how it is graded and attributed, the four discrimination tests it must survive, and how a refuted assertion is dispositioned without deletion.

findings.name: Evidence basis, discrimination tests and false-positive disposition
findings.description: Every declared dependency records its basis (modelled artefact, written agreement, cited legal act, interview, observed telemetry, statistical association), an evidence grade, an asserting agent possibly acting on behalf of another, and an assertion time held separately from the observation time. It also records the outcomes of four discrimination tests: ownership is not dependency, sequence is not causation, correlation is not a declared dependency, and obligation is not reliance. Assertions supported only by association are downgraded to candidate rather than published. Refutation is a disposition on the assertion, retained rather than deleted. This model records the disposition and emits attribution entries; the enforcement, risk-scoring and audit-trail engines that consume them are owned elsewhere.

questions.text: What is the basis of this assertion, and what evidence grade does that basis carry?
answer_data: Evidence grade code and grading rule version
References to the cited items with their versions

questions.text: Who asserted the dependency, on whose behalf, and at what assertion time as distinct from the observation time?
answer_data: Asserter reference and delegating party where applicable
Assertion time in RFC 3339 with offset
Observation or ingestion time where it differs

questions.text: Which discrimination tests were run for ownership, sequence, correlation and obligation, and what were their outcomes?
answer_data: Resulting status of declared, candidate or refuted

questions.text: What observation would falsify this dependency, and has that check actually been performed?
answer_data: Reason where the check is impracticable

questions.text: What review interval or trigger applies, and how is a refuted assertion dispositioned without deleting it?
answer_data: Supersession reference where a replacement assertion exists

data_elements.name: Evidence basis code
data_elements.description: Coded basis of the assertion: modelled artefact, written agreement, cited legal act, interview, observed telemetry, or statistical association.

data_elements.name: Evidence grade code
data_elements.description: Grade assigned to the strongest supporting basis under the profile's grading rule.

data_elements.name: Asserter reference
data_elements.description: Agent that made the assertion, with any delegating party recorded separately.

data_elements.name: Assertion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion was made, in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the underlying condition was observed or the record ingested, recorded whenever it differs from the assertion time.

data_elements.name: Discrimination outcome set
data_elements.description: Structured outcomes of the ownership, sequence, correlation and obligation tests, each with reason and tester.

data_elements.name: Disposition code
data_elements.description: Current disposition of the assertion: declared, candidate, withdrawn, refuted, expired, or superseded.

artifacts.name: Dependency declaration evidence pack
artifacts.description: The compiled set of references and test outcomes supporting one declared dependency at one review point: cited artefacts with versions, discrimination-test results, falsification criterion and check result, asserter attribution, and the resulting disposition. It is a compiled record for review, not an audit trail; audit-trail storage, immutability and review remain with the adopting Dimension's audit model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the assertion identifier from the authoritative master system holding the dependency record, plus a monotonic review sequence number per assertion. Where no master system governs the assertion, a Dimension-assigned ULID is used and marked Dimension-local. The review instant is metadata; it never serves as the identifier.

functions.name: Declare a typed socio-operational dependency
functions.description: Record one canonical dependency assertion between a dependent endpoint and a depended-on endpoint under a published kind, with applicability qualifiers, at least one evidence entry and an attributed asserter.
outputs: Canonical dependency assertion in draft or declared state
Validation report listing any profile violations
preconditions: The kind profile is published and its version resolves
Both endpoint references resolve in their owning master systems
The direction matches the profile's canonical direction
No existing assertion shares the same canonical tuple
effects: Creates an assertion and binds it to the profile version used
Records asserter identity and assertion time distinct from observation time
Changes nothing in the real-world arrangement, process, contract or staffing that the assertion describes

functions.name: Propose a dependency kind for a candidate reliance
functions.description: Given a candidate reliance statement and its endpoint types, propose the socio-operational kind that fits, or report that no published kind fits.
outputs: Unresolved-typing note where no kind fits
preconditions: The kind profile registry is readable
Endpoint types are stated or derivable from the endpoint references
effects: Produces a proposal only and never publishes an assertion
Escalates ambiguous or unfitting cases to the kind steward
Records the typing rationale for later review

functions.name: Validate endpoints, direction and cardinality against the kind profile
functions.description: Check an assertion against its declared kind profile for endpoint type conformance, direction, cardinality, cycle permission and transitivity behaviour.
inputs: Kind profile at the cited version
Existing assertion set for cardinality and cycle evaluation
outputs: Ordered list of violations with the constraint breached
preconditions: The assertion set in scope is readable
effects: Marks the assertion conformant or non-conformant
Blocks publication while violations remain
Performs no remediation and alters no endpoint record

functions.name: Screen a candidate assertion for false positives
functions.description: Apply the four discrimination tests, ownership versus dependency, sequence versus causation, correlation versus declared dependency and obligation versus reliance, and record their outcomes.
inputs: Ordering evidence such as a modelled flow or event ordering
outputs: Outcome per discrimination test with reason
Status recommendation of declared, candidate or refuted
preconditions: At least one evidence entry exists
The reference data needed for each applicable test is reachable or the test is marked not performed
effects: Records test outcomes on the assertion
Downgrades to candidate any assertion supported only by association
Computes no risk score, criticality rating or impact severity

functions.name: Bind temporal, spatial and jurisdictional applicability
functions.description: Attach the applicability qualifiers under which an assertion holds: interval relation and lead time, location or site binding, and jurisdiction with its citing instrument.
inputs: Temporal interval or required lead time
Location or site code with code list version
Jurisdiction code, reference frame and citing instrument identifier
outputs: Applicability qualifier set bound to the assertion
Report of qualifiers that could not be resolved to a governed code
preconditions: Code lists and instrument identifiers resolve at a stated version
Interval bounds are expressed with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
effects: Narrows the validity of the assertion to the bound qualifiers
Marks the assertion expired when a bound window closes
Does not alter the underlying arrangement, authorisation, site or schedule

functions.name: Compile a third-party dependency register extract
functions.description: Produce a read-only extract of conformant supplier and third-party assertions for one reporting scope, mapped to a target register schema.
inputs: Target register schema and field mapping
outputs: Register extract artifact with sequence number and content digest
preconditions: All in-scope assertions are conformant to their kind profiles
Party identifiers required by the target schema are present or explicitly reported as absent
effects: Produces an immutable extract bound to the profile version used
Does not submit the extract, notify any authority, or interpret the supervisory obligation the extract serves
Leaves the underlying assertions unchanged

functions.name: Disposition a withdrawn, refuted, expired or superseded assertion
functions.description: Close out an assertion with an explicit disposition and reason while retaining a tombstone that records the kind and both endpoints.
outputs: Supersession link where a replacement exists
preconditions: The acting party holds the reviewer role for the scope
A reason is supplied and the disposition code is valid for the current state
effects: Retains the record and marks it withdrawn, refuted, expired or superseded
Never performs a hard delete, so consumers can distinguish never asserted from no longer asserted
Leaves retention periods and any physical erasure to the adopting Dimension's records and privacy models

composition.target: Host subject record of the adopting Dimension (any world-model entry that can carry dependencies)
composition.purpose: Attach typed socio-operational dependency assertions to a host subject without altering the host's own identity, lifecycle or semantics, following the pattern of qualified relations attached to an entity.

composition.target: Generic typed-relationship mixin of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Specialize a general non-causal influence relation into named socio-operational kinds. Only the kind semantics, endpoint constraints and discrimination tests are specialized here; generic edge identity, versioning and conflict machinery remain in the general mixin.

composition.target: Technical and system dependency taxonomy (adjacent split of WM-XCT-037)
composition.purpose: Cross-reference component, interface and data-flow dependency edges so that a socio-operational assertion about a provider can be linked to, without absorbing, the technical dependency graph.

composition.target: Organization and party register model (W3C ORG aligned, LEI-backed)
composition.purpose: Resolve actor endpoints and read structural, membership and consolidation facts used by the ownership discrimination test. Structural mastering, post lifecycle and ownership records stay with the register.

composition.target: Process model repository and procedure model
composition.purpose: Resolve activity endpoints and read modelled flows used as evidence for process reliance. Process authoring, versioning and execution stay with the repository.
Carry citations to duties, clauses and legal acts and record the asserted deontic class, without holding rule text, fulfilment state, remedies or interpretation.

composition.target: Third-party arrangement and outsourcing register model
composition.purpose: Resolve arrangement endpoints and receive the register extract produced here. Arrangement mastering, supervisory obligation and any submission stay with that model.

composition.target: Business impact analysis, continuity and risk models
composition.purpose: Supply declared dependencies and their evidence as inputs to impact and risk work. Severity, criticality scoring, recovery objectives, risk evaluation and treatment remain owned there.

composition.target: Records management, privacy and audit models of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Receive retention periods and erasure instructions and hand over attribution entries. Retention setting, erasure execution and audit-trail integrity and review are owned there, not here.

composition.target: UN/CEFACT Buy-Ship-Pay Reference Data Model vocabulary
composition.purpose: Align resource and counterparty strands so that a payment or settlement reliance is distinguishable from a delivery reliance and from a contractual reliance on the same party. Alignment is by mapping only; no conformance is claimed.

composition.target: Time Ontology in OWL interval relations
composition.purpose: Map temporal reliance codes to the standard interval relations for topology only. The alignment target asserts no causation, so no causal reading is inherited. Cited as a Candidate Recommendation Draft, so conformance is not claimed.

composition.target: ESCO occupations, skills and competences classification (ISCO-mapped)
composition.purpose: Bind capability and competence endpoints to governed concept identifiers instead of free-text role names, with a local extension path where no governed concept exists.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one accountable owner package for dependency kind profiles; an assertion citing a kind that no package owns must be rejected, not defaulted.

The owner package must publish, for each kind, its endpoint types, canonical direction, cardinality, cycle and transitivity behaviour, applicability conditions, required evidence grade and false-positive tests before any assertion using that kind is accepted.

The owner package must record which neighbouring model masters each endpoint type and must not redefine those endpoints locally; an endpoint type with no named owning model is a gap, not a local definition.

Where a kind expresses a regulatory concept such as a critical or important function or a chain of activities, the owner package must record the citing instrument, its version and the jurisdiction in which it applies, and must not present the concept as globally applicable.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Kind identifiers, evidence grades, discrimination outcomes and disposition codes are minted in a Dimension-controlled namespace. Never mint identifiers inside a standards body's namespace and never reuse an external IRI as a local kind identifier. External vocabularies are attached by explicit mapping entries that name the external term, its version and the point at which the alignment ceases to hold, so that a revision of the external vocabulary cannot silently change local semantics.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 (record plane world-model, nav path NAV.XCT.DEP, entry kind mixin)
Party endpoints: the Global LEI system for ISO 17442 legal entity identifiers
Capability endpoints: the ESCO classification with its ISCO mappings
Legal and jurisdictional citations: the European Legislation Identifier register, used as a citation mechanism rather than as a source of doctrine
Location and trade-strand vocabulary: the UN/CEFACT web vocabularies including UN/LOCODE

canonicalization_rules: An assertion canonicalizes to the tuple (dependent endpoint reference, kind identifier with profile version, depended-on endpoint reference, applicability qualifier set); two records with the same canonical tuple are the same assertion and must be merged rather than duplicated.

Endpoint references canonicalize to the authoritative master-system identifier held by the owning model; display names, free-text party names and local aliases are non-canonical and are ignored when testing equality.
Direction is canonical: every assertion is stored dependent to depended-on as declared by the kind profile. Inverse views are derived at read time and are never stored as a second assertion.
All time values canonicalize to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; a known UTC instant whose local offset is unknown uses the -00:00 form rather than Z.
Code values canonicalize to the code plus the code list identifier and version; a bare code without its list version is not canonical.
patch_rules: Changing the kind, either endpoint, or the direction is not a patch: supersede the assertion and create a new one carrying an explicit supersedes link and a reason.

Applicability qualifiers, evidence entries, discrimination outcomes, substitutability measures and disposition may be patched in place, each with a new assertion time; prior values must remain retrievable.
A patch must never rewrite an existing evidence entry's basis or asserter; a correction is added as a new evidence entry with a correction reason referencing the superseded entry.
A patch that would leave the assertion non-conformant to its cited profile version is rejected; migrate to a new profile version instead.
compatibility_rules: Adding a kind, an evidence grade, a disposition code or an optional qualifier is backward compatible. Narrowing endpoint types, tightening cardinality, flipping canonical direction or removing a kind is breaking and requires a major profile version plus a migration mapping.
Consumers must ignore unknown optional qualifiers, and must reject rather than coerce an assertion citing an unknown kind identifier or an unknown profile version.
Alignment mappings to external vocabularies are versioned independently of the kind profile, so an external revision never silently alters local kind semantics.
Assertions retain the profile version under which they were made; re-validation against a newer profile is an explicit, recorded operation, not an implicit upgrade.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record that owns the endpoint or the assertion, for example the arrangement identifier in the contract or supplier master, the organizational unit identifier in the organization register, or the process element identifier in the process repository.

Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system identifier governs the endpoint: an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier for a party, an ESCO concept IRI for a capability, an ELI URI for a legal act, or a UN/LOCODE-derived location code, each recorded with its scheme and version.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension only when neither of the above exists; it is marked Dimension-local and must never be presented as an external or authoritative identifier.
A reporting reference date, effective date, review date or as-at instant is never an identifier under any circumstances; dates and instants may only qualify an already identified record.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds precision and an explicit numeric offset or the Z designator; bare local times and offset-less values are invalid. Event time (when the relied-on condition, arrangement, ordering or change actually occurred) is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time (when the condition was seen, and when the assertion was made or loaded); where these differ, all differing values must be present and individually labelled, and a known UTC instant with an unknown local offset uses -00:00 rather than Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely register extracts and evidence packs, are named <artifact-kind>-<owning-scope-identifier>-<zero-padded monotonic sequence>-<kind-profile-version>. The sequence is monotonic within its scope and is the only ordering key; gaps must be explained. The reporting or review instant travels as metadata beside the name and never substitutes for the sequence, and no date component appears in the name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonical form, the kind-profile version it was produced under, and the asserter or compiler identity. A consumer must reject an artifact whose digest fails to verify, whose profile version is unknown, or whose endpoint references do not resolve in the owning master systems, and must report the rejection rather than silently degrading to a partial read.

policies: No assertion without a basis: a declaration must carry at least one evidence entry and recorded outcomes for every applicable discrimination test before it can move beyond draft or candidate status.

Reference, do not restate: obligations, organizational structure, process models, arrangements, impact assessments and risk ratings are referenced by governed identifier; their text, lifecycle, consequences and scores are never copied into this model.
Kind before instance: an assertion may only use a dependency kind whose profile is published and versioned, and it is bound to the version in force when it was made.
No silent refutation: a dependency shown to be false is dispositioned as refuted with a reason and retained, so that consumers can distinguish never asserted from no longer asserted.

No execution: this model never triggers or authorises workflow execution, procurement, contract award or termination, staffing changes, payments, supervisory submission, enforcement or legal decisions.

Declare the frame: every regulatory concept, jurisdiction reference and chain-scope claim records the instrument, version and jurisdiction it comes from; no jurisdiction's doctrine is treated as the default.

read: Read by dependent endpoint, by depended-on endpoint, by kind, by applicability window, by evidence grade and by disposition; multi-hop traversal is permitted only for kinds whose profile declares transitivity, and is otherwise blocked with an explanatory error.
Register extracts and evidence packs are read-only projections; reading never mutates the underlying assertions or their review state.

A read that resolves endpoint references must honour the access rules of the owning model and must not widen them; where an endpoint is not readable by the caller, the assertion is redacted or withheld rather than dereferenced.
Reads always return the profile version an assertion was made under, so a consumer can detect stale semantics.
create: Creation requires a published kind identifier with version, both endpoint references resolving in their owning master systems, direction consistent with the profile, at least one evidence entry, an asserter reference, and an assertion time in RFC 3339 with an offset.
Creation is rejected as a duplicate when the canonical tuple already exists; evidence is added to the existing assertion instead.
Creation of an assertion supported only by statistical association is admitted at candidate status only and cannot be published as declared.
Creating a kind profile requires the kind steward role and a complete endpoint, cardinality, cycle, transitivity, applicability, evidence-grade and false-positive-test declaration.
update: Kind, endpoints and direction are immutable; any change to them requires supersession with an explicit supersedes link and reason.

Applicability qualifiers, evidence entries, discrimination outcomes, substitutability measures, review schedule and disposition may be updated, each recording a new assertion time and preserving the prior value for retrieval.
Updating an assertion never updates the endpoint records it references; endpoint corrections are made in their owning models and re-resolved here.
A profile version change is applied to existing assertions only by an explicit, recorded re-validation operation.
delete: Assertions are not hard-deleted in the ordinary course. A withdrawn, refuted, expired or superseded assertion is dispositioned and retained as a tombstone carrying the kind identifier, both endpoint references, the disposition code, the reason and the disposition instant, so consumers can distinguish never asserted from no longer asserted.

Minimum retention for tombstones and superseded versions is set by the adopting Dimension's records-management policy and by any external register obligation that an extract populates; this model states the requirement to retain but does not set, calculate or enforce the period.

Physical erasure, including erasure demanded by personal-data rules where an assertion names an individual post holder, is executed by the adopting Dimension's records-management and privacy models. This model exposes the affected assertion set, accepts an erasure instruction from the owning policy, and records that erasure occurred by reason code, retaining a non-identifying tombstone only where that governing policy permits.
A kind profile must not be deleted while any assertion references it; deprecate the version and migrate assertions instead.
Register extracts and evidence packs are immutable once issued; a defective artifact is superseded by a later sequence number and marked defective, never deleted in place.

roles.name: Dependency kind steward
responsibilities: Own, publish and version kind profiles including endpoint types, direction, cardinality, cycle and transitivity behaviour and applicability conditions
Approve breaking profile changes and the accompanying migration mapping
Maintain external alignment mappings and record where each alignment stops
Adjudicate typing proposals that no published kind fits

roles.name: Dependency asserter
responsibilities: Declare assertions with at least one evidence entry and an attributed asserter
Run and record the applicable discrimination tests before requesting publication
Record event time separately from observation and assertion time where they differ
Escalate rather than force-fit a reliance that no published kind covers

roles.name: Endpoint data owner
responsibilities: Master the referenced party, process, capability or arrangement records in the owning model
Guarantee that endpoint identifiers remain resolvable and notify on retirement, merger or reissue
Confirm the access rules that assertions referencing those endpoints must inherit

roles.name: Dependency reviewer
responsibilities: Perform scheduled and triggered reviews of declared assertions
Apply the falsification criterion and disposition refuted assertions with a reason
Remain independent of the asserter for assertions supporting critical or important functions

roles.name: Register compiler
responsibilities: Produce reporting-scope extracts with sequence number, profile version and content digest
Verify mandatory target-schema fields and report unmapped or unavailable fields explicitly
Refrain from submitting extracts or interpreting the supervisory obligation they serve

roles.name: Access custodian
responsibilities: Apply scope rules, redaction and masking for sensitive sub-tier identities and named post holders
Grant, time-bound and review access exceptions with a recorded justification
Hand attribution entries to the audit model without asserting ownership of the audit trail

access.default_rule: Least privilege by scope and by endpoint: reading an assertion requires read permission on both endpoint records in their owning models. Where the caller may read only one endpoint, the assertion is returned reduced to the kind and the permitted endpoint, or withheld entirely, according to the adopting Dimension's disclosure policy; this model never widens the access rules of a referenced model.
exceptions: A supervisory or contractual disclosure obligation may compel release of a register extract beyond the normal scope; the exception is recorded with the citing instrument, its version and the requesting authority, and the release itself is executed by the model that owns the reporting obligation.

Break-glass read of dependency assertions supporting critical or important functions may be granted during a disruption for a bounded period, with an explicit expiry instant and mandatory post-hoc review.

Commercially sensitive substitutability assessments and sub-tier party identities may be masked from general internal readers while remaining visible to the kind steward, the reviewer and the register compiler.
Assertions naming an individual post holder are restricted to the smallest necessary audience; the capability-level or post-level assertion is the default disclosed form.
audit_requirements: Every create, supersession, disposition, profile change and access-exception grant emits an entry carrying actor identity, acting-on-behalf-of where applicable, reason, and an RFC 3339 instant with seconds and an explicit offset. This model produces these entries; storage, immutability, retention and review of the audit trail are owned by the adopting Dimension's audit and records models.
Extract production records the kind-profile version, reporting-scope key, sequence number and content digest so that any issued extract can be reproduced or shown to be irreproducible.
Access to masked sub-tier identities and to assertions naming individual holders is logged with the stated justification and reviewed periodically by the access custodian.
Downgrades from declared to candidate and all refutations record the discrimination test that caused them, so that false-positive rates can be assessed by the owning quality function.

read_order: AGENTS.md first: resolve Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any read or write, including when the projection is MongoDB or MCP
Specification URL: model purpose, scope statement, in-scope and out-of-scope lists and boundary notes, so that target-owned concepts are not modelled locally
Kind profile registry URL: the published kinds with their endpoint types, direction, cardinality, cycle and transitivity rules, applicability conditions and false-positive tests
Storage type URL and Interface URL: projection and access mechanics only; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections and carry no semantics
Processes URL: declaration, validation, review, supersession and disposition procedures including the role required for each
Bootstraps of the neighbouring models that master the endpoints (organization and party register, process repository, contract and arrangement models) before asserting any edge against them

coverage.claim: This split delivers a defensible socio-operational dependency taxonomy for WM-XCT-037: nine bounded findings covering process, capability, organizational, supplier, contractual, legal, financial, temporal, spatial and jurisdictional reliance, each with declared direction, endpoint constraints, cardinality, applicability, evidence and false-positive tests, grounded in seventeen live primary sources from eight independent organizations. It does not claim conformance to any cited standard, does not cover technical or system dependency, and does not own impact computation, risk evaluation, enforcement or audit-trail semantics.

checklist.notes: Four-tier identity priority headed by the authoritative master-system identifier, then governed global identifiers (ISO 17442, ESCO IRI, ELI URI, UN/LOCODE-derived codes), then Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID, with an explicit prohibition on dates as identifiers. Endpoint identity is resolved in the owning model, never minted here.

Draft, candidate, declared, withdrawn, refuted, expired and superseded states with immutable kind, endpoints and direction; changes to those require supersession. The lifecycle of the endpoints themselves (posts, arrangements, contracts) is explicitly left to the owning models.

Per-kind endpoint type sets, canonical direction with derived inverses, cardinality, cycle permission following the withdrawal of the reportsTo acyclicity claim, and explicit transitivity flags that block multi-hop inference by default.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z throughout; event time separated from observation and assertion time; Allen interval relations for temporal reliance topology; required lead time and validity interval as first-class qualifiers.

Asserter with acting-on-behalf-of, evidence basis codes, evidence grade, cited instrument versions, and the non-causal influence framing that prevents a provenance link from being read as a dependency.

Ownership of the depended-on record is recorded separately from reliance, and the ownership discrimination test uses accounting-consolidating-parent data specifically to prove that a control relation is not a dependency. Package ownership and role ownership are set in the dimension layer.

Profile conformance validation for endpoints, direction, cardinality and cycles; four discrimination tests with recorded outcomes; a falsification criterion per assertion; blocked publication while violations remain.

Least privilege requiring read on both endpoints, redaction where only one endpoint is readable, four declared scopes, and four bounded exception classes for supervisory disclosure, break-glass, commercial sensitivity and named individuals.

No hard delete in the ordinary course; tombstones carry kind, both endpoints, disposition and reason. Retention periods are set by the adopting Dimension's records policy and any external register obligation, and physical erasure is executed by the records-management and privacy models, with this model only exposing affected sets and recording a reason code.

Alignment mappings to BPMN constructs, W3C ORG properties, ODRL deontic classes, PROV influence, OWL-Time interval relations, UN/CEFACT strands and ESCO concepts, each versioned and each carrying an explicit point at which the alignment stops. No conformance is claimed.
Ten reliance kinds grouped into work and capability, actor and agreement, and resource and situation, each with its own endpoint rules rather than a single untyped edge.
Evidence basis codes and grades, mandatory falsification criterion, downgrade of association-only assertions to candidate, and reviewer independence for critical or important functions.

Substitutability, concentration and reliance-share measures are declared as data elements, but no consulted primary source prescribes a scale or threshold. DORA and the FSB toolkit require assessment without defining a metric, so the adopting Dimension must supply and version its own scale; treat the current measures as uncalibrated.
Jurisdiction is a first-class qualifier with a named reference frame and a governed citation mechanism, and all regulatory examples are marked as instrument-specific rather than universal.
Site and location reliance is bound to governed location codes with code list versions and a relocation sensitivity flag; facility mastering stays with the facility model.

Handled by reference: masking of sub-tier identities and named post holders is specified as an access exception, while cryptographic and platform controls belong to the adopting Dimension's security model.
Declaration, validation, screening, applicability binding, extract compilation and disposition are specified as non-executing functions; no function initiates real-world action.

known_omissions: No dependency-strength or criticality scale is defined; the model deliberately stops at declaring reliance and its evidence, leaving severity and criticality to the impact and risk models.
Impact propagation across multi-hop chains is not modelled, because transitivity is a per-kind property here and propagation semantics belong to the impact model.
Reciprocal and mutual dependency (two parties each relying on the other) is expressible as two assertions but has no dedicated kind; whether it warrants one is unresolved.
Collective-action dependencies such as reliance on an industry utility, standards body or shared infrastructure consortium are typed only as party reliance and may need a distinct kind.
Informal and cultural reliance (tacit knowledge, goodwill, undocumented accommodation) is admitted only at candidate status, so it is systematically under-represented relative to contracted reliance.
Regulatory-approval sequencing dependencies internal to a licensing process are not typed; they are treated as jurisdictional reliance plus temporal relation, which may be too coarse.

No accessible primary source was obtained for ISO business continuity terminology (iso.org returned HTTP 403), so BIA framing rests on NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and the FSB toolkit; the ISO alignment is asserted only through RFC 3339's ISO 8601 profile and ISO 17442 via GLEIF.

The UN/CEFACT alignment rests on the web vocabulary landing page (BSP RDM D23B); the element-level class and property definitions were not retrieved, so strand mappings are structural rather than element-precise.
The BPMN citation is to the specification landing page; the normative clause text was not retrieved, so flow semantics are used at the level of the construct distinction only.
conflicts: Scope conflict: the CSDDD chain of activities excludes product disposal and, for regulated financial undertakings, downstream activities, while DORA's ICT third-party scope carries no equivalent carve-out. A single 'supply chain dependency' kind cannot satisfy both, so chain scope must be declared per assertion with its citing instrument.

Definitional conflict: EBA/GL/2019/02 separates outsourcing from other third-party arrangements such as purchase of goods, whereas DORA's register covers ICT services more broadly. The same arrangement can be inside one register and outside the other, so arrangement type and target register are recorded independently.

Structural conflict: W3C ORG explicitly removed the informative claim that org:reportsTo is acyclic, while many escalation and approval kinds are designed on an acyclicity assumption. Cycle behaviour is therefore declared per kind and never assumed.

Semantic conflict: PROV models influence rather than causation, while operational practice routinely reads a dependency edge as causal. This model does not license the causal reading and requires a separate blocking-mode statement instead.

Status conflict: the current /TR/ version of the Time Ontology in OWL is a Candidate Recommendation Draft rather than a Recommendation, so its interval relations are used as an alignment target and no conformance is claimed.

Granularity conflict: DORA's critical-or-important-function test is function-scoped and materiality-based, whereas supplier registers are arrangement-scoped. An assertion must therefore carry both the supported function and the arrangement, and neither may be inferred from the other.
regional_assumptions: DORA, CSDDD, the EBA guidelines, ELI and ESCO are European instruments used as worked examples of dependency typing, not as globally applicable requirements; an adopting Dimension outside the EU must bind local equivalents.
NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 and SP 800-34 Rev. 1 are US federal guidance cited as practice evidence, not as requirements outside that context, and SP 800-34 Rev. 1 dates from 2010.
'Third country' in DORA is EU-relative; every jurisdictional reliance therefore records its reference frame rather than assuming a default home jurisdiction.
ESCO maps to ISCO but remains European in coverage; non-European adopters should bind a local occupational and competence scheme through the alignment mapping.

No consulted source is authoritative on common-law versus civil-law contractual doctrine, on agency, or on privity; the model records citations and reliance facts and deliberately imports no interpretive doctrine.
The FSB toolkit is explicitly cross-jurisdictional but non-binding, so its terminology is used for comparability rather than as a compliance basis.
adversarial_checks: Ownership test: substitute a wholly owned subsidiary that supplies nothing. If the assertion survives, it was a control or consolidation edge misfiled as a dependency; GLEIF Level 2 data is the reference for the test.

Sequence test: reorder the two activities in simulation. If the dependent activity still completes, the edge recorded ordering rather than reliance, and BPMN flow type plus interval relations must be recorded instead of a dependency.
Correlation test: if the only basis is historical co-occurrence, the assertion is capped at candidate status. PROV influence does not license a dependency claim.
Obligation test: remove the cited duty and ask whether operational failure still follows. If it does, reliance is independent of the obligation and both facts must be recorded separately.
Scope-collision test: a provider inside a DORA register but outside a CSDDD chain of activities must not be collapsed into one generic supply chain kind; the assertion must name its scope instrument.
Transitivity test: assert A to B and B to C, then query A to C. Unless the kind profile declares transitivity, the inference must be refused rather than silently returned.

Boundary sweep: every finding and function was checked for executing verbs (approve, terminate, pay, hire, procure, submit, enforce, score). None appears as an effect; the closest case, the register extract, explicitly does not submit and does not interpret the obligation it serves.

Ownership-of-neighbour sweep: audit trail, retention period, erasure execution, impact severity, recovery objectives and risk evaluation each appear only as a reference or boundary note, never as a local capability.
